sentences.en: A few years ago, Fred DeJesus from Brooklyn, New York became the first umpire in a minor league baseball game to use something called the Automated Ball-Strike System (ABS), often referred to as the ‘robo-umpire’.
sentences.zh: 几年前，纽约布鲁克林的弗雷德·德赫苏斯成为首位在小联盟棒球赛中使用自动好坏球判定系统（ABS）的裁判。人们常把这套系统叫作“机器裁判”。

sentences.en: Instead of making any judgments himself about a strike*, DeJesus had decisions fed to him through an earpiece, connected to a modified missile-tracking system.
sentences.zh: 德赫苏斯无需自己判断是不是好球。判定结果通过耳机传给他，耳机与一套经过改装的导弹跟踪系统相连。

sentences.en: The contraption looked like a large black pizza box with one glowing green eye; it was mounted above the press stand.
sentences.zh: 这套装置像一个黑色的大披萨盒，上面有一只发绿光的“眼睛”；它装在记者席上方。

sentences.en: Major League Baseball (MLB), who had commissioned the system, wanted human umpires to announce the calls, just as they would have done in the past.
sentences.zh: 美国职业棒球大联盟（MLB）委托开发了这套系统，它希望仍像过去一样，由真人裁判宣告判定结果。

sentences.en: When the first pitch came in, a recorded voice told DeJesus it was a strike.
sentences.zh: 第一个球投来时，录制好的语音告诉德赫苏斯，这是个好球。

sentences.en: Previously, calling a strike was a judgment call on the part of the umpire.
sentences.zh: 以往，判一个球是不是好球，要由裁判自行判断。

sentences.en: Even if the batter does not hit the ball, a pitch that passes through the ‘strike zone’ (an imaginary zone about seventeen inches wide, stretching from the batter’s knees to the middle of his chest) is considered a strike.
sentences.zh: 即使击球手没有打中球，只要投球穿过“好球区”，也就是一块约17英寸宽、从击球手膝盖延伸到胸部中央的假想区域，这一球就算好球。

sentences.en: During that first game, when DeJesus announced calls, there was no heckling and no shouted disagreement.
sentences.zh: 在那场首秀中，德赫苏斯宣告判定时，没人起哄，也没人高声抗议。

sentences.en: Nobody said a word.
sentences.zh: 谁也没说一个字。

sentences.en: For a hundred and fifty years or so, the strike zone has been the game’s animating force—countless arguments between a team’s manager and the umpire have taken place over its boundaries and whether a ball had crossed through it.
sentences.zh: 大约150年来，好球区一直是让棒球比赛充满活力的因素：球队主教练和裁判就它的边界在哪里、某一球究竟有没有穿过这个区域，争论过无数次。

sentences.en: The rules of play have evolved in various stages.
sentences.zh: 比赛规则经历了多个阶段的演变。

sentences.en: Today, everyone knows that you may scream your disagreement in an umpire’s face, but you must never shout personal abuse at them or touch them.
sentences.zh: 如今大家都知道，你可以对着裁判的脸大声表达异议，但绝不能破口辱骂裁判，也不能碰裁判。

sentences.en: That’s a no-no.
sentences.zh: 那可是大忌。

sentences.en: When the robo-umpires came, however, the arguments stopped.
sentences.zh: 然而，机器裁判一出现，争论就停了。

sentences.en: During the first robo-umpire season, players complained about some strange calls.
sentences.zh: 使用机器裁判的第一个赛季，球员对一些奇怪的判定颇有怨言。

sentences.en: In response, MLB decided to tweak the dimensions of the zone, and the following year the consensus was that ABS is profoundly consistent.
sentences.zh: 为此，大联盟决定微调好球区的尺寸。到了第二年，人们普遍认为，ABS的判罚尺度高度一致。

sentences.en: MLB says the device is near-perfect, precise to within fractions of an inch.
sentences.zh: 大联盟称，这套设备近乎完美，误差只有一英寸的几分之一。

sentences.en: “It’ll reduce controversy in the game, and be good for the game,” says Rob Manfred, who is Commissioner for MLB.
sentences.zh: 大联盟总裁罗布·曼弗雷德说：“它会减少比赛中的争议，对这项运动有好处。”

sentences.en: But the question is whether controversy is worth reducing, or whether it is the sign of a human hand.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，争议值得减少吗？抑或争议正是人参与其中的体现？

sentences.en: A human, at least, yells back.
sentences.zh: 至少，真人还会回吼一声。

sentences.en: When I spoke with Frank Viola, a coach for a North Carolina team, he said that ABS works as designed, but that it was also unforgiving and pedantic, almost legalistic.
sentences.zh: 我同北卡罗来纳州一支球队的教练弗兰克·维奥拉交谈时，他说，ABS的运行符合设计预期，但它也毫不通融，死抠细节，简直像在生搬硬套法律条文。

sentences.en: “Manfred is a lawyer,” Viola noted.
sentences.zh: 维奥拉指出：“曼弗雷德是律师。”

sentences.en: Some pitchers have complained that, compared with a human’s, the robot’s strike zone seems too precise.
sentences.zh: 一些投手抱怨说，与真人裁判划定的好球区相比，机器裁判的好球区似乎精确过了头。

sentences.en: Viola was once a major-league player himself.
sentences.zh: 维奥拉自己也曾是大联盟球员。

sentences.en: When he was pitching, he explained, umpires rewarded skill.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，当年他当投手时，投球技术好就会得到裁判的认可。

sentences.en: “Throw it where you aimed, and it would be a strike, even if it was an inch or two outside.
sentences.zh: “只要投到你瞄准的地方，就会被判好球，哪怕偏出好球区一两英寸。

sentences.en: There was a dialogue between pitcher and umpire.”
sentences.zh: 投手和裁判之间有一种对话。”

sentences.en: The executive tasked with running the experiment for MLB is Morgan Sword, who’s in charge of baseball operations.
sentences.zh: 摩根·斯沃德主管大联盟的棒球事务，也负责为大联盟开展这项试验。

sentences.en: According to Sword, ABS was part of a larger project to make baseball more exciting since executives are terrified of losing younger fans, as has been the case with horse racing and boxing.
sentences.zh: 斯沃德说，ABS是一项更大计划的一部分，目的是让棒球比赛更精彩；高管们之所以这样做，是因为他们非常害怕失去年轻球迷，赛马和拳击就曾有过这样的遭遇。

sentences.en: He explains how they began the process by asking fans what version of baseball they found most exciting.
sentences.zh: 他解释说，他们的第一步是问球迷：什么样的棒球比赛最让他们兴奋？

sentences.en: The results showed that everyone wanted more action: more hits, more defense, more baserunning.
sentences.zh: 结果显示，所有人都想看到更多场上动作：更多的安打、更多的防守，还有更多的跑垒。

sentences.en: This type of baseball essentially hasn’t existed since the 1960s, when the hundred-mile-an-hour fastball, which is difficult to hit and control, entered the game.
sentences.zh: 这种棒球比赛自20世纪60年代以来基本上就消失了。正是在那个年代，时速100英里、既难打中又难控制的快速球进入了赛场。

sentences.en: It flattened the game into strikeouts, walks, and home runs—a type of play lacking much action.
sentences.zh: 这种快速球使比赛变得单调，剩下的多是三振、四坏球保送和本垒打，场上很少有其他动作。

sentences.en: Sword’s team brainstormed potential fixes.
sentences.zh: 斯沃德的团队集思广益，寻找可能的解决办法。

sentences.en: Any rule that existed, they talked about changing—from changing the bats to changing the geometry of the field.
sentences.zh: 只要是已有的规则，他们都讨论过能不能改，从更换球棒到改变球场的几何形状都考虑过。

sentences.en: But while all of these were ruled out as potential fixes, ABS was seen as a perfect vehicle for change.
sentences.zh: 不过，这些备选方案全都被排除了，而ABS被视为实现变革的理想手段。

sentences.en: According to Sword, once you get the technology right, you can load any strike zone you want into the system.
sentences.zh: 斯沃德说，技术一旦调试到位，你想要什么样的好球区，都可以把它载入系统。

sentences.en: “It might be a triangle, or a blob, or something shaped like Texas.
sentences.zh: “它可以是个三角形、一团不规则的形状，或者可以长得像得克萨斯州的版图。

sentences.en: Over time, as baseball evolves, ABS can allow the zone to change with it.”
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，棒球会发展，ABS也能让好球区随之变化。”

sentences.en: “In the past twenty years, sports have moved away from judgment calls.
sentences.zh: “过去二十年间，体育运动越来越少依赖裁判个人的判断。

sentences.en: Soccer has Video Assistant Referees (for offside decisions, for example).
sentences.zh: 足球有视频助理裁判，例如用来协助判定越位。

sentences.en: Tennis has Hawk-Eye (for line calls, for example).
sentences.zh: 网球有鹰眼系统，例如用来判定球的落点是否在线内。

sentences.en: For almost a decade, baseball has used instant replay on the base paths.
sentences.zh: 棒球在跑垒线路上的判罚采用即时回放，已有近十年。

sentences.en: This is widely liked, even if the precision can sometimes cause problems.
sentences.zh: 尽管这种精确有时会带来问题，这样的做法还是广受欢迎。

sentences.en: But these applications deal with something physical: bases, lines, goals.
sentences.zh: 但这些技术处理的都是实物：垒包、界线、球门。

sentences.en: The boundaries of action are precise, delineated like the keys of a piano.
sentences.zh: 场上动作的边界很精确，就像钢琴上的琴键那样划分得清清楚楚。

sentences.en: This is not the case with ABS and the strike zone.
sentences.zh: ABS和好球区的情形却并非如此。

sentences.en: Historically, a certain discretion has been appreciated.”
sentences.zh: 历来，人们都很看重留给裁判的那一点裁量空间。”

sentences.en: I decided to email Alva Noë, a professor at Berkeley University and a baseball fan, for his opinion.
sentences.zh: 我决定给伯克利大学的教授、棒球迷阿尔瓦·诺埃发邮件，听听他的意见。

sentences.en: “Hardly a day goes by that I don’t wake up and run through the reasons that this [robo-umpires] is such a terrible idea,” he replied.
sentences.zh: 他回复说：“我几乎每天一醒来，都会在心里过一遍，想想为什么这件事［指采用机器裁判］是个糟糕透顶的主意。”

sentences.en: He later told me, “This is part of a movement to use algorithms to take the hard choices of living out of life.”
sentences.zh: 后来他告诉我：“这是当下某种趋势的一部分：人们试图用算法，让生活中那些难以作出的抉择消失。”

sentences.en: Perhaps he’s right.
sentences.zh: 也许他说得对。

sentences.en: We watch baseball to kill time, not to maximize it.
sentences.zh: 我们看棒球是为了消磨时间，可不是为了把时间利用到极致。

sentences.en: Some players I have met take a dissenting stance toward the robots too, believing that accuracy is not the answer.
sentences.zh: 我遇到的一些球员也反对使用机器裁判，他们认为，判得精确并不能解决问题。

sentences.en: According to Joe Russo, who plays for a New Jersey team, “With technology, people just want everything to be perfect.
sentences.zh: 效力于新泽西州一支球队的乔·鲁索说：“有了技术，人们就想让一切都尽善尽美。

sentences.en: That’s not reality.
sentences.zh: 现实可不是这样。

sentences.en: I think perfect would be weird.
sentences.zh: 我倒觉得，事事完美会很奇怪。

sentences.en: Your teams are always winning, work is always just great, there’s always money in your pocket, your car never breaks down.
sentences.zh: 你的球队总是赢，你的工作总是顺风顺水，口袋里一直有钱，车子也从来不抛锚。

sentences.en: What is there to talk about?”
sentences.zh: 那还有什么可聊的？”
